content.text:
The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. It has no lodash imports, and `Row`, `Config` and the three exported signatures are unchanged.

**Checks:**
- **Behaviour:** a randomized comparison (20,000 cases within the input ranges) against the `es-toolkit/compat` implementations matched on all three functions. For `applyPatch` I used an array-by-index overwrite and nested-object patch case, not random patches. Lodash itself isn't installed here, so compat stood in as the reference.
- **Types:** `tsc --strict` passes on the file.
- **Size:** `npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 1962 bytes (min+gzip) and 113 bytes of own code. I couldn't measure the original, because `src/module.ts` imports lodash and lodash isn't installed. So I can't confirm the own-code allowance against the original.

**Function mapping:**

| lodash | es-toolkit | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `merge` | `merge` (strict) | Same behaviour in this input range: it mutates and returns `base`, and arrays merge by index. |
| `startCase` | `startCase` from `es-toolkit/compat` | Strict `startCase` lowercases the rest of each word, so `YY` becomes `Yy` and `YZ` becomes `Yz`. Compat keeps the lodash result. |
| `fromPairs` | `zipObject` (strict) with a small adapter | It gave 553 bytes against 607 for compat `fromPairs` in a trial with strict `startCase`. Duplicate keys still resolve to the last value. |

The adapter is `zipObject(pairs.map(p => p[0]), pairs.map(p => p[1]))`. It adds about 28 bytes of own code over compat `fromPairs`. If the own-code allowance turns out tight, switching `toLookup` to compat `fromPairs` is the one-line trade-off.

Most of the size comes from compat `startCase`. It is the only es-toolkit option that preserves the behaviour for inputs with consecutive capitals.
